request: How large is the immigration court backlog and how has it changed over time?

reply.reply:
**At the end of FY2024, the immigration court backlog stood at 3,558,995 pending cases; caseloads have generally risen since 1983, with annual receipts increasing much more rapidly since FY2019.**

- At the end of FY2024, EOIR had 3,558,995 pending immigration court cases. (IN12492, PDF p. 4)
- Although immigration judges completed a record 701,749 cases in FY2024, EOIR received an average of 148,663 new cases per month that year. (IN12492, PDF p. 4)
- Immigration court caseloads have generally increased since EOIR began in 1983, with much faster growth in annual case receipts since FY2019 except during FY2020 and FY2021. (IN12492, PDF p. 2)
reply.reasoning: The CRS report gives the backlog count at FY2024 year-end and describes the historical trend in case receipts. In FY2024, judges completed a record number of cases, but monthly receipts were substantially higher than monthly completions.
